description.text: Every hundred years the Dark Lord rises in the Obligatory Tower, and Thistlewick sends somebody north to put him down. It has worked forty-seven times. You are the Forty-Eighth, selected while you were asleep and therefore unable to object.
The tower door is open. At the top of the stairs is a Dark Lord, and the Prophecy is very clear about what happens next. It has been clear about it forty-seven times.
The Dark Lord was never the problem. The Prophecy was, and it has been annulled. Clause twelve has been struck from the records and replaced with a note reading SEE BRAM.

Prudence Thrupp and her sister Dorcas have not spoken for thirty years. It is not a falling-out. They stopped one day and neither of them started again, so they send each other things instead. This one is a jar. Do not shake it. Do not ask what is in it.
Dorcas has sent something back. It is heavier than the jar was. Considerably heavier. Do not open it, do not shake it, and do not let it near a fire.
Dorcas sent back something worse than the jar, deliberately, and Prudence laughed. Thirty years, and her sister has still got it. She is going to write to her at the weekend. Do not tell Dorcas.

You cannot be an adventurer in this district unregistered. You can do the adventuring. You just cannot be one. Registration takes Form A-1, which requires a character reference, a hat, and Form A-1. Form A-1 has been mislaid for eleven years.
Registered: a Guild Card (Provisional). In forty years nobody had brought Registrar Pell all three at once. The board is open to you, and so, administratively, is a mound with a curse on it.
THE CRAB OF UNUSUAL SIZE. Holds the west beach. Will not be reasoned with. Has been there longer than the town. Everyone in Nether Sopping is very careful to say 'unusual'.
The Crab of Unusual Size no longer holds the west beach. Four smaller crabs hold it now, between them, badly. Its card says DISCHARGED, in Pell's hand.
M. CROOKE, BANDIT CHIEF. Camp in the western hills. Runs a six-week banditry apprenticeship with a syllabus.
Meredith Crooke's bounty is discharged, and somebody has pinned her syllabus up next to the card as a curiosity. Her pass rate this year was ninety per cent.

The light has been out since the spring, for want of oil. It is not for the ships. There have been no ships for ninety-one years. It is for the ones coming back down the north road at night: you can see it from the crossroads, and it is what you walk home by.
The lighthouse at Nether Sopping is lit. Out on the north road, at the crossroads, there is a light in the south again when you turn round.

objectives.text: Get a gallon of lamp oil

description.text: Two crowns to look into the Bottomless Pit, a wonder of the district, which is four feet deep. Something has moved in down the far end and has been eating the lost property: two hundred years of it.
It was a badger. Fenwick Splint told the Guild for forty years, and they never came and saw the badger. Admission is free for you now. Forever.
A Scheduled Monument of the district, entry restricted to registered adventurers. Underneath, in chalk, in a much older hand: THERE IS A CURSE ON IT AS WELL.
Ambrose Fitch, the Forty-Fourth, waited forty years to have that fight, and it took four minutes. He gave you the grave goods, rather than letting you take them, which he was particular about.
Forty years of standing in a circle, and what he wants is a bench. Top of the mound, facing the sea, where people walking the north road tired can sit down. Anyone's bench. Not his. Anyone's.
A bench on the top of the barrow, facing the sea. Anyone may sit on it, which was the point. One piece was left over, which is traditional.

objectives.text: Put a bench on the mound

description.text: Hosea is compiling A Complete And Accurate History Of The Obligatory Quest. Complete is going well. Accurate is the problem. Everyone in the Slain Wyvern has been on one, and not one of them will tell a historian. They will tell you.
Complete. Not accurate - two of the tales cannot both be true on a Tuesday - but complete. The Footnote on page four hundred and one is you. It says you listened.

objectives.text: Hear six tales, to the end

description.text: Halbert Quy went north thirty years ago, and came back, and asked a question at the next meeting. His cottage was ready by the Friday. Forty-seven Chosen Ones did the sword, he says, and not one of them ever asked the man why he doesn't stop. Ask him why. Then listen to the whole answer.
You told him what Grimspite said, all of it, in order, including the part about the tea. It took most of an afternoon.

Lift has never been the problem. The Hoyle Works can get anything off the ground; they have had a shed off the ground. They come down, in sight of the tower. Ott Hoyle has one variable left she has never been able to get hold of, and it walked into her works this morning and asked whether they had a gift shop.
Attempt Two Hundred flies. She is outside the gate. Do not set her down on anything with a roof on it.

The works stores book has been kept honestly since 1802, and everything ever issued has a line through it but one: ITEM 1, issued 199 times, returned 198. Attempt 199 is on a crag in sight of the tower, and everything aboard her is intact.
ITEM 1 is off the crag, in a crate, and is not light.
Ott rendered ITEM 1 down, and was visibly relieved to have it out of a field. Nobody has yet ticked it off.
ITEM 1 was set down in front of the throne, and the Dark Lord was delighted. It was the first new thing in four thousand years.

A machine that spent a hundred and forty years repairing itself out of its neighbours, still faintly trying to go north, has stopped. She got further than any of them, Ott says. There is a bay in the shed with her number over it, and she is coming up the hill.

Spare Cotterill, aged nine, would like to come. He has asked every Chosen One who ever walked up that street, and been told he cannot. The Parish Office issues the form, and his mother signs it, or nobody does.
Spare Cotterill, aged nine: Form P-9, countersigned by his mother. He is coming. He has to write.
A tutorial, in a meadow, run by Fizz, who is extremely pleased to see you. There are four stations. Everything is explained, at least twice, in capitals.
Graduated: the first completed tutorial on record. Fizz said so, several times, in capitals.

objectives.text: Get a stick from Old Hollis

description.text: The Guild says a meadow has to have a fetch quest, so Dilys Fenwick's sheep are lost. A bit. They are just there. They are pigs. They have been practising their baa.
Dilys Fenwick's sheep, which are pigs, have been found, where they were. They look extremely found.
Check your quest log so that you don't have to remember really hard.

Mr Hollowell keeps the Former Premises, and its visitors' book, which has never had a visitor in it. He would very much like the incumbent's signature. The book never leaves its lectern, so he has given you a slip, ruled to match.
NAME: GRIMSPITE THE INEVITABLE. FROM: HERE. REMARKS: Never been. Heard marvellous things about the lift.

Clause eleven: a Chosen One is certified fit before departure. It has been done forty-seven times. Bram's form is blank, because he was asleep. Merribell will now do it. Properly. She needs the form, a pair of stamped scales, a good light and a witness.
Bram is certified fit to travel under clause eleven, properly, with a witness. The Certificate of Fitness does nothing. It is very properly filled in.

objectives.text: Use the form, with a witness

description.text: Tobias Frayne has been brought back eleven times. Merribell will not make it twelve. There is nothing wrong with him, which is the trouble, and the cure is to leave.
Tobias Frayne has had the parish to tea, twice, and nobody fell off anything. The twelfth line in his book is empty.

Sump has been under a curse since 1794. Nobody there has drunk a glass of water since. Mr Thurle says it is a very thorough curse. Merribell says it is a very thorough thirst, and has re-formed the Water Committee to deal with it.
The curse on Sump is lifted, on a motion of the Water Committee, re-formed. Sump has had a glass of water.

Instead of the eleventh symposium - Whether Anything Works, at three - Merribell has proposed the queue at the gate: twenty patients each half, and whoever is through first is right. Sister Bewick wants it in writing.
The question was settled by the queue at the gate instead of by the eleventh symposium, and Whatever Works won, on points. Sister Bewick has it in writing.
The Table sits in the back room of the Slain Wyvern: medics only, who have kept the parties alive and have stories about it. Merribell is on the list.
The Healers' Table sat, with Merribell on the list, and she told them to write it down. They have given her the Table's Kit.
A tube plate for the Two Hundred's refit, forty-one holes, made at Ollerenshaw's in one heat, by four hands. Neither smith finished a sentence. It wants carrying up the hill to Ott.
The Two Hundred's tube plate was made in one heat, by four hands, and Ott tried every hole with a gauge pin. True, every one. That will do, she says. They will know what she means by it.

objectives.text: Take the plate up to Ott

description.text: Somebody has stolen the anvil out of Hob's smithy. They will not have got far.
The anvil is back in Hob's smithy, to the inch. Two apprentices failed module seven, acquisition of a heavy object, by eleven feet. The apology is on the back of a syllabus, in a very good hand.
Beatrice Grumnir's grave has no marker of Hob's making. He is very large at being at a loss. He will make one at the forge, and carry it over, and see.
Thistlewick churchyard has a new gate, with a good latch. Somebody says the latch wants a spring.

The Worshipful Company of Smiths will examine a smith's best work, under clause one, if it is shown with everything else he has made, under clause two. Hob has made a great deal, and given all of it away. Eleven owners, three towns, and Nix.
The Worshipful Company of Smiths disqualified Beatrice under clause one, and Hob beamed. The Wardens' notes say she is right about everything.

objectives.text: Go back to the Prime Warden

description.text: The Sky Anvil is star-iron. Hob made Meech a gate for it, out of the eleven gates in the hedge-bottom, and the gate is a very good gate. The star-iron wants taking home to the forge.
Hob made one sword out of the Sky Anvil's star-iron, and he will not say who it is for.

objectives.text: Take it home to the forge

description.text: Three hedge mages, nine years without a name, in an igloo in a lay-by. Dunnock taught himself out of a book with four pages missing, and is better than the Collegium at exactly those four. He taught Zephyrine page twenty-three, badly, and it works.
NOTICE OF OUTSTANDING FINES (ELEVENTH), Miss Z. Vance, on study leave. The first ten went to her pigeonhole. She was not on study leave. She was EXPELLED.
There was never an expulsion: only a draft, referred to a committee that has never met.
There was never an expulsion, and the fines are paid. Zephyrine Vance is a member of the Collegium in good standing.
There was never an expulsion, so she asked for one. The draft is filed, at her own request, and she is expelled at last, properly.

objectives.text: Settle it, one way or another

description.text: On the Kindling of Damp Materials, by Dr Hapgood, went out under the Master's name, and the Master is a committee. Zephyrine said so at High Table, once. She has now demonstrated it. Everybody is fine. The room was wrong.
Congregation is quorate at twelve: eleven Fellows who come to things, and one who is a duck. Every meeting for eleven years has been inquorate. The duck is on a pond, some way off.
Congregation was quorate for the first time in eleven years, with all twelve Fellows present, one of them a duck. Carried. The duck's proxy is hers.

She was expelled for an unsanctioned quantity of fire. The Commissioner had a form. QUANTITY OF FIRE: nine hundred acres. SANCTIONED, three times. It burned all afternoon and all night, and the road is dry.
Eleven things have been in Nix's ledger since the beginning with nothing in the RETURNED column. This is the afternoon they go back: three towns, eleven owners, and none of them aware it had gone.
The ledger is ruled off. Hulda Bole gave Nix something better: a parcel, for a client not yet identified.

Enoch Bagshawe, first bassoon to the Upper Clanging Works Band, has one reed that took three weeks, and it goes the moment anything looks at him. He would like to cross the Gloamwood by night. Nix halves encounters. Half an encounter is still an encounter.
Enoch Bagshawe crossed the Gloamwood by night without a single encounter, or half of one. The Works Band has a bassoon.
The parcel was a letter in Nix's own hand: NOT TO BE OPENED UNTIL I AM TWENTY-SIX. The client is Nix, aged fifteen, and there is a ticket for Bond No. 1, in Great Dunnage.
Bond No. 1 was her gran's coat, too long for her at fifteen, not to be worn until it fitted. It fits.
The Door of the Sealed Counting House is open, informally. Form L is not completed. The Opening proper will follow on its completion. The Mayor has gone in at something close to a run.
Behind the Door of the Sealed Counting House there is one chair, and a note: WE SPENT IT. J. Pocklington, Clerk to the Corporation, 1788. It is a very good chair.

Cobb Lorrimer, registered under T, says locating is stealing with a waistcoat on. The challenge is a client, a list and an afternoon. The client is Sops and Tibb. The list is in a child's hand: ONE ROPE. ONE HELMIT. ONE SWORD. ONE DARK LORD (WHO LOSES).
Nix won Cobb Lorrimer's challenge on paperwork: the whole list located, with permission, and receipts.

Nobody had asked Sir Aldric about his horse in six years, including Sir Aldric. She walked into Plummer's yard one winter with a good saddle on and nobody in it, and she is a partner in the haulage business now. She is doing so well. He may visit any day but a Tuesday.

The committee could not fault his nine pins, and so had to fault the knight, and offered him a desk and a pin that does not move. He said it was the finest thing he had been offered in nine years, and no. Knight Errant, At Large: they made it up for him, on a Thursday.
TO THE PARISH OF LITTLE GORE. BY HAND. P-G. His father gave it him the morning he rode out: four miles, your first errand, deliver it and then you may go errant. He has been errant for nine years.
The letter to the Parish of Little Gore is delivered, by hand, nine years late. He may now go errant.

Pemberton-Gore the Fourth found Little Gore first time, and would like to squire. He can find gates. Every other Pemberton-Gore came over the wall; his uncle went OUT. He walks three paces behind now, and says if his uncle is facing the wrong way. He always is. It's on the arms.
Dusk to dawn, in the right chapel at last - he had kept vigil in eleven wrong ones. Sir Hamo Tench sat at the back and coughed. Confirmed: the first in thirty years.

Eight years ago he was sent to slay a dragon and arrived at a different one, and they talked about Horace for four hours. Horace was a poet. He was talking about his horse. The right dragon was slain by somebody else. This one was read to, and the commission reported on, on its back.
There is no rhyme for turnip. Everybody had a go, and every suggestion was worse than the last. Piper changed the other line, in nine seconds, and everybody who spent the afternoon on it is furious.

The Committee keeps a box of verses it struck and never printed. To consult it takes Form S-7, countersigned, and the key on Councillor Fenn's hook. Nobody is listening to Councillor Fenn. Remember him.
The box was opened, and shut again, and the key went back on the hook. Piper has read every verse in it, and printed none.

objectives.text: Get the key off Fenn's hook

description.text: The Contest at the Sign of the Bell is always tonight; they have simply not had the entries. Nobody has ever entered Ballad (Not Sad). Piper Quill is aware of that.
Second place in Ballad (Not Sad), by one point, to a thrush. The certificate is framed.

Abel Thrush carried the post between Little Gore, Fenmarch and Sump every day for fifty years. Somebody has nailed a card to the back of the fingerpost, where nobody reads but a chronicler. Everybody knew him, and each of them knew him differently.
An elegy for Abel Thrush, the carrier: nine lines, pinned up, and not performed.

Ambrosine Quill, Chronicler to the Committee, has finished THE LAY OF THE FORTY-EIGHTH. The Committee approved it on Tuesday. Bram has not finished yet. The shape has. It is in four cantos of twelve, and there is no turnip in any of them.
Piper read it again, and found it very good. One footnote, in small type: None of this happened. It is very good. - P.Q.
THE LAY OF THE FORTY-EIGHTH, fixed, in metre, in an afternoon, by A. & P. Quill.
No curse. A very good sword in very poor condition, with a name on the tang nobody has used for a while. He asked what a curse would cost to have put on. It is not expensive. There is a form.
One name on Ashcombe's Roll is marked Away. (Written to.) Two hundred and six people stood on a hill in the rain and counted him anyway. Today, then.
His mother has a new kitchen, his room is a study, and the speech at the Flood Dinner went well. Nothing went wrong. There is a scarf.
The lake is let down once a year, for the sluices, and that week you can walk the street at the bottom. His grandfather made the sword. It was the doorstop.
Under the lake, in a strongbox in the schoolroom, the schoolmistress kept everybody's reports. His says he will go far, if he ever gets up.
The league table: 17. C. ASH 0 (no meetings attended). Seventeenth, of seventeen, behind Blackwood, and Blackwood is NEW. Points are scored at meetings.
Corvin Ash has attended a meeting, and is second in the league table. His chair is kept.

Eleven years ago, for two crowns, she told him he was the rival of a great hero. She tells about four young men a year, because it is the reading that makes them stand up straight, and it has never once been wrong. They all went and did something.
Wren was asked to leave the Slain Wyvern for saying that the wyvern is a goose. It is a goose. She would like a retraction. Dorcas will read a second plaque. Engraving is a crown a letter.
A second plaque, on the other side of the fire. It neither corrects the first nor repeats it.

objectives.text: Put it up, with Wren there

description.text: Wren has named a small brown thing in Bram's turnip field after him, and then explained why. It is statistically indefensible. It has a labelled stick.
The Gloamwood Society has discussed The Sighting four times a year since 1960, and once a year it goes for a walk. Wren is going with them, and would like a proper look.
The Thing in the Gloamwood is proved not to exist. Miss Pellow counted nine, in 1971. She was right.

A monograph of the Collegium requires a type specimen for every entry, three Fellows to review it, and a list of subscribers. Rowbotham named three hundred species and never had a type specimen for one of them. He named them after his dogs.
Wren Halloway's monograph of the Collegium is published, and on the shelf, in the inch-wide gap.
Mrs Puddifoot dusts all eighty specimens, Friday to Wednesday, and has asked a proper naturalist, with the jars, to authenticate them. Dr Rowbotham named everything. That was the problem.
Fenmarch's cabinet of eighty specimens is written up, honestly, every join of it, and the family has paid the fee.
The sword Roland carries has a mark on it, and Hob knows the mark. It was made at the forge in Thistlewick forty years ago, and sold, and travelled, and came back. She did good work, Hob says.
The sword was made at the forge in Thistlewick forty years ago. It is back, on an ash haft, as an axe, in a Thistlewick hand.
THE FAIRWEATHER ALUMNI: eleven parties who finished their quests without him, at dinner, in the Slain Wyvern, at capacity. Every one of them says 'our Roland'.
Eleven parties drank to Roland Fairweather, who got them all to the door. The card on the board is signed eleven times.
The snug at the Bell is booked in his name. The usual. Roland went slightly pink, and asked you not to say anything.
The hundred and forty-first meeting. The stone is not ready. The asset is available. Noted, with thanks. Eleven minutes.

Maud Penhallow, sixteen, has been in Fellow Blunt's yard since she was nine: sword, horse, lineage, the lot. She has been told it is nearly ready. Roland was told that when he was twelve. He does not know whether to tell her.
He told her. She asked whose. She has gone north.

WHEN THE STONE IS READY, ONE OF THE LINE SHALL DRAW THE SWORD THEREFROM, AND GO DOWN UNDER CARN DREY. He knows it by heart. Fellow Blunt checks the stone quarterly, from the gate. Nobody has gone down the stairs to look. GONE TO SEE.
The sword is out of the stone, and the Worm of Carn Drey is ended. Discharged.

His mother's third term was: you write. The post is a courier in a red coat, who is already standing in every town when you get there and never explains. Spare writes the letters. They do not have to be true.
Read out to the shift at the dinner hour. There was no dragon. His mother did more potatoes anyway.

objectives.text: Go home for the dinner hour

description.text: Effie Gotobed of Much Pottering has been his pen pal since he was six. She told him about a volcano and a sea serpent. He told her he drives the Two Hundred. They knew each other at once, and they are both furious about it.
Effie showed Spare round Much Pottering, and they each wrote one letter on the spot. The courier carried them four steps.
Something is on the paddle of the bottom lock, thirty boats are sat on the cut, and the Canal Company's smallest man went in at eleven and has not come out. A man does not fit. Spare fits.
Spare went into the bottom lock alone, in the dark, and came out by the ladder, and everybody was there. Thirty boats went down the cut.
Dear Mam. Is it spring yet? Spare. He asks every morning as well.
Dear Mam. Is it spring yet? It is. Spare cannot miss this.
It is spring, and every Cotterill in Upper Clanging is indoors today.
Ten Cotterills. The new one is called Washer. Clevis had it at twenty to one, and has had to pay out.
With the Committee's congratulations on your return: your pension, and the key to a cottage at Nether Sopping, at such distance as is mutually agreeable. They trust Friday will suit.
The cottage was Ambrose Fitch's. There is a chair facing the window, a bed you may use, and a pot with a dead thing in it. You do not have to live there.
NO ADMITTANCE WITHOUT A LAMP. Sir Dunstable has lent you the lamp off the hook. Behind the Door into the Mountain is a stair going down into a dark that does not stop.
His chalk marks go down the walls, D. 1 at the Door, each a little further down than the last.
At the bottom of the Stair, past the last of Sir Dunstable's marks, was something nobody had anticipated. It has been met.
It wrote a bounty on itself, and wanted it stamped. A bounty is claimed by a member, in person, at the Guild's desk. The card has no authority and no number, and a drawing of an octopus on the back.
Form Z, Matters Not Anticipated. Registrar Pell had kept it forty years, in case. DISCHARGED.

objectives.text: Take the card to the Guild
